subject: SIG: Source integrity, deploy guardrails, and ephemeral secrets — evidence package
messages:
From: Lina Morris <lina.morris@questaudit.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sig-requests@fin-assess.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG evidence request: source integrity & deploy guardrails

Karthik —

As part of the SIG assessment for Cobalt Financial (in-scope systems), we need an evidence bundle that demonstrates Redwood's secure SDLC controls focused on source integrity, CI/CD gating, secrets handling (ephemeral credentials), and change/deploy approvals. Can you provide the following by July 7th? A condensed package is fine — we will request raw logs if needed.

Requested items (high level):
- Description + current configuration for code review / branch protection (how merges are blocked, required approvers)
- Sample PR validation evidence (build + pre-merge checks) — ideally 3–6 redacted examples with timestamps
- CI workflow snippets showing gating steps (lint/unit/tests/dependency scanning / SBOM generation if present)
- Evidence that secrets used in pipelines are ephemeral and rotated (policy + one audit log entry showing a rotation event)
- Deploy approval trail for at least two production deploys (who approved, timestamp, commit id — redaction acceptable)
- Any automated guardrails (preflight checks, canary stage gating, automatic rollback triggers)

If there are standard artifacts you prefer to send (zipped report, Drive link), that's fine. Also let us know if you prefer a short call to walk through the package.

Thanks,
Lina Morris
Senior Assessor, QuestAudit
lina.morris@questaudit.com

---
This request is part of SIG intake HUBSPOT-88921.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morris <lina.morris@questaudit.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG evidence request: source integrity & deploy guardrails

Lina —

Thanks for the clear list. We assembled an initial evidence package and attached the most relevant artifacts below. I am copying Monica (engineering security) and Aditya (platform infra) for technical details and to coordinate any follow-ups.

Attached in this thread:
- pr-validation-report-2025-06-30.pdf — consolidated pre-merge validation results for a sample set of recent PRs (redacted author email addresses, retains PR number, pipeline run id, and timestamps).
- ci-workflow-yaml-snippets.txt — excerpted CI workflow steps that show required jobs for PR gating (lint, unit, dependency-scan, signature verification). Sensitive runner tokens removed.
- ephemeral-vault-policy.json — our Vault policy describing time-to-live (TTL) for ephemeral credentials used by CI runners and deploy agents, and the rotation process.
- deploy-approval-log.csv — produced from our deployment orchestration service; each row includes deploy_id, target_env, approver (internal id), approval_time, and the committed source reference (we can redact full SHAs on request).

Quick highlights:
- Code review + merge gating: branch protection enforces at least one code review approval and CI success. Critical modules require security approval as an additional reviewer via CODEOWNERS. Merge to main is blocked if any status checks fail.
- PR validation: pre-merge pipeline is enforced by server-side webhooks and cannot be bypassed for protected branches. The attached report covers 6 PRs across core services (all show blocked merges until CI success).
- Secrets management: CI and deploy agents use short-lived tokens provisioned from Vault; tokens are issued per-job with TTLs between 10–60 minutes depending on sensitivity. We have attached the policy and can pull the vault audit entry for a rotation event if needed.
- Deploy guardrails: deploys to prod require an approve action in the orchestration UI; we have canary stages and automatic health-check-based rollback configured. The log gives approver ids and timestamps for two recent prod deploys.

If you need raw pipeline run logs or the Vault audit entry for a specific rotation event, we can provide a redacted export or a Drive link. We can also set a 30m walkthrough — I have availability Wed 7/2 afternoon or Thu 7/3 morning (PST).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: pr-validation-report-2025-06-30.pdf, ci-workflow-yaml-snippets.txt, ephemeral-vault-policy.json, deploy-approval-log.csv
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morris <lina.morris@questaudit.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG evidence request: source integrity & deploy guardrails

Lina / Karthik —

Adding a few implementation details that often help assessors:
- PR/merge rules: we require a minimum of one non-author approver for all PRs. For modules marked HIGH_RISK via our module registry, we require one security approver. These checks are enforced by GitHub branch protection plus a server-side pre-receive hook that verifies the PR validation token.
- PR validation tool: we use an internal preflight runner that signs validation results with a short-lived key. The attached PDF includes the signature status column; each PR record shows that the signed artifact was verified by the pre-receive hook.
- CI gating: the snippets file shows the job ordering and explicit 'must_pass' gating for security scans and SBOM generation (where applicable).
- Ephemeral secrets: the Vault policy included documents the TTL for job tokens and describes automated rotation on credential expiry. We have an audit trail entry (vault-audit-2025-06-25.log) which we can export; it shows a rotation event for the deploy agent used on 2025-06-25 at 02:17 UTC.

If the assessor prefers, I can drop a redacted version of the vault audit entry into the Drive link Karthik mentioned (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/SDLC/2025/PR_validation_pack).

Thanks — happy to jump on the call to walk through the package and point to the exact pipeline run ids.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Engineering Security
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Lina Morris <lina.morris@questaudit.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: sig-requests@fin-assess.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG evidence request: source integrity & deploy guardrails

Karthik / Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — I started a pass through the PDF and snippets. A couple quick clarifications before we accept the package:
- Can you provide one vault audit log entry that shows a rotation event (timestamp + actor) for the token used by your deploy agent? A redacted line with the rotation event id is sufficient.
- For one of the deploys listed in deploy-approval-log.csv, can you include the commit reference used for that deploy (a redacted SHA is fine; we only need to confirm commit immutability mapping to the build artifact).

If you can drop those two items in the Drive link (or attach here) we'll mark this request as complete and schedule a short call to go through any questions. We could do a 20–30m call Tue 7/1 10:00–10:30 PDT if that works.

Appreciate it,
Lina
Senior Assessor, QuestAudit
lina.morris@questaudit.com
